subject: Post-call recap + architecture choices: toolflow & SDK/auth/rerank
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acmehealth.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + architecture choices: toolflow & SDK/auth/rerank

Hi Alice / Tom — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap of the discovery and three concrete architecture options so we can align on a path for the PoC.

Summary of needs we heard:
- PHI-sensitive patient data (HIPAA) and strict data residency controls.
- Target interactive latency: 150-250ms p50 for UI flows; batch/async allowed for heavy indexing.
- High-quality semantic search + re-ranking for clinical note retrieval, plus structured tool-calling to downstream billing/EHR APIs.
- Customer wants to evaluate hosted flow first, but expects a path to private/dedicated deployment.

Architectural options (tradeoffs):
1) Hosted Redwood API + Private Workspace (fastest PoC)
   - Pros: quick onboarding (SDK + keys), streaming responses, managed embeddings + reranker, built-in observability.
   - Cons: requires strong VPC/KMS isolation and contractual controls for PHI; network egress considerations.
2) Dedicated Capacity in Redwood (reserved GPUs in our infra)
   - Pros: predictable throughput, can isolate model variants, lower per-token unit cost at scale.
   - Cons: longer lead time to provision; heavier commit.
3) Hybrid (on-prem retrieval + hosted generation)
   - Pros: retrieval of EHR data stays in your network; hosted models do generation/rerank.
   - Cons: added orchestration and routing complexity.

Tool/function-calling patterns we recommend for PoC:
- Tool definitions: keep them explicit and small surface-area. Examples: ehrSearch(query, patient_id, filters) -> returns list of doc refs; scoringService(doc_ids, query) -> returns scores; billingLookup(account_id) -> returns billing status.
- Tool choice: prefer a two-stage flow for retrieval + ranking: fast vector search (top-N) then a lightweight pairwise reranker for final ordering.
- Parallel tools: run embedding-based retrieval and a cached keyword fallback in parallel; merge results and de-dupe before rerank. This reduces tail latency when dense index misses.
- Error handling: fail-open semantics for non-critical tools (analytics, enrichment); fail-closed for PHI access controls. Add idempotent retries (exponential backoff) and circuit-breakers for downstream APIs. Have a deterministic fallback model (smaller LLM) when the primary model is degraded.

Recommended PoC approach (my suggestion):
- Phase 0: Hosted PoC on Redwood Private Workspace with scoped data (de-identified subset) + SDK integration for your web UI.
- Phase 1: Add dedicated capacity or private deployment if latency/SLA and PHI contracts require it.

Requested inputs from ACME to proceed:
- Confirmation on latency SLO and monthly volume estimate (requests/day, avg tokens per request).
- Data retention and encryption requirements (KMS/HSM preference).
- Which downstream tools we need to model for the PoC (EHR search, billing, patient-lookup API) — list owners and endpoints if possible.

Attachments: redwood-toolflow-options-v1.pdf (detailed diagrams), sketch-toolflow.png (whiteboard sketch).

Next steps:
- If you’re happy with Phase 0 we’ll provision a sandbox workspace and share an SDK sample repo + minimal config for OIDC/KMS.
- Can we target a 30–45 min tech-walkthrough next week? I’m proposing Tue 5/18 10:00–10:45 PT — let me know if that works.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake

Jordan — really helpful write-up, thank you. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Priority #1 is PHI isolation. Our InfoSec would prefer Private deployment eventually, but we understand trialing hosted with strong contractual controls could speed evaluation.
- Latency SLO: we need p50 < 250ms, p95 < 800ms for interactive retrieval flows. Batch indexing jobs can be async.
- Tools to model in PoC: ehrSearch (internal ES endpoint), clinical-reranker (we can provide a scoring container if useful), billingAPI (external partner).
- We have an existing OIDC provider (Okta) and a customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS).
- Budget: tight for Q2 — PoC must stay low-cost; if we like results, we can discuss committed capacity for Q3.

Can you confirm whether the two-stage retrieval (dense vector -> pairwise rerank) will fit within our p95 target if the reranker is hosted? If not, we may need on-prem for reranking. Also please send the SDK sample and any light config we can review.

Tue 5/18 10:00 PT works for Tom and me. Please send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Alice Chen
Director, Product — ACME Health

Looping in a couple quick engineering notes we can attach to the PoC package. I sketched an SDK/config example and added a small snippet (see sdk-snippet.txt). Key calls:

- SDK bootstrap (JS pseudo):
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, workspace: 'acme-poc', region: 'us-west-2' })
  // optional routing override for hybrid: client.setRouting({ retriever: 'local-proxy', generator: 'redwood-hosted' })

- Auth pattern: use Okta OIDC for developer authentication + short-lived mTLS tokens for service-to-service. Customer-managed AWS KMS for encryption-at-rest; Redwood supports external KMS integration in Private/Dedicated.

- Routing: policy-based routing (header + path) is simplest. Example: X-RW-Instance: "acme-poc" directs requests to the private workspace. For hybrid retrieval, route /retrieval to your local proxy that returns doc ids, then call Redwood for reranker/generation.

- Structured output/tool-calling: define a strict tool schema and validation in the SDK. Example output: {"tool": "ehrSearch", "args": {"patient_id": "123", "filters": {...}}, "confidence": 0.88} — Redwood will enforce input/output shapes for the PoC if you want.

- Embeddings & reranker: store canonical embeddings in your VPC-hosted index (FAISS or Pinecone) and use Redwood to compute query embeddings. For latency, compute query embedding locally (if network is the bottleneck) and send small vectors to our reranker service. Pairwise reranking should be limited to top-10 candidates to stay within p95 targets.

Attached: sdk-snippet.txt (small code examples). Happy to expand into a runnable repo for Tue's call.

—Marissa
